desc: What business the chair announces next, and when a scheduled item may seize the floor: priority queues with preemption plus calendar gates. Acts between questions (feeding the engine) except special orders at their hour and scheduled recess/adjournment, which interrupt a pending question.

temporal_frame.hierarchy: meeting is a subset of session; session = unit of scheduling freedom [8:1-2, 8:11-12]
temporal_frame.quarterly_interval: sessions <= a quarterly interval apart form a corridor through which business travels by postponement, tabling, unfinished business, or pending reconsider; beyond it (or across a membership-term boundary) only committee referral carries business over [9:7-10, 21:7(c)]
temporal_frame.horizon: no order of the day may be set beyond the next regular session (within the corridor), or beyond the present session (outside it) — guard/schedulable-to [14:6, 41:40]
temporal_frame.no_binding_future_majorities: one session may not bind a later session's majority except via special rules/bylaws [8:12-14]

made_by: agenda position without stated hour or with guidance-only hour
agenda hour assignment (adopted with the agenda)

item_kinds.desc: reserves a meeting; taken up right after minutes approval; outranks all other special orders regardless of when made
not schedulable directly; arises from prior meeting per carryover

standard_order_of_business.status: a rule of order; alterable per rules.json

queues.unfinished-business: (a) question pending at last adjournment, (b) unreached unfinished business from last meeting in its prior order, (c) unreached general orders from last meeting in made-order [41:21-23]
queues.general-orders-current: made-order; same-motion batches in listed order [41:23, 41:52]
queues.reports: standing committees in bylaws-listing order; special committees in appointment order [41:13, 41:17]
queues.chair_discipline: the chair announces items; he must not ask 'is there unfinished business?' but state the known next item [41:24]; he cannot unilaterally depart from the order [41:39]

dispatch.NOTE(judgment): this is a synthesis of [41:18-27, 41:40-57] into one procedure; RONR states it distributively — each step cites its source. Holds against the worked examples [41:51, 41:55].
dispatch.desc: Between questions, at heading special-orders onward: first step whose when expression is true governs. These expressions are the compiled body of guard/order-of-day-due.

steps.note: taken up right after minutes approval

steps.select: among those whose hour has arrived or passed, minimum made_at

steps.take_up: a general order whose hour has arrived
next item by heading order through the queues
new business: members introduce in floor-obtained order (event/recognized)

preemption.desc: The compiled body of guard/may-preempt(item): a special order at its hour interrupts a pending question EXCEPT for the listed yields; scheduled recess/adjournment hours are declared by the chair even mid-special-order.

special_order_at_hour.yields: (a) motions relating to adjournment/recess, (b) questions of privilege, (c) a special order made earlier, (d) the special order for the meeting
special_order_at_hour.resumption: interrupted business resumes afterward at the point of interruption (lifecycle history restore) — earliest-made special orders first, then the originally interrupted business [41:55, 18:11]

preemption.scheduled_recess_adjournment: chair announces and declares it, even mid-special-order; pending business is interrupted (recess) or carried per carryover (adjournment). Preemptible only by a two-thirds motion to postpone the hour or extend consideration time; announced previous-question-ordered votes may customarily be completed first [20:6-7, 21:14, 41:56, 41:66-68]
preemption.enforcement: any single member may demand conformance via motion/call-for-orders-of-the-day; the demand compels the schedule unless set aside — two-thirds NEGATIVE on 'proceed to the orders of the day', or two-thirds affirmative to extend time / suspend and take up something else [18:4(7), 18:8]. Once refused, not renewable until the pending business is disposed of [18:8(a), 38:7(3)]. Except when a special order must be taken up, the call itself yields to the making or calling up of a reconsider [18:4(1)] — a due order of the day does not outrun the reconsider window.
preemption.early_take_up: only by reconsidering the making vote (while possible) or suspend-the-rules (two-thirds) [14:13, 41:40]; equivalently, laying intervening items on the table one at a time is a legitimate majority path [17:14, 41:38]

carryover.case: adjournment not ending session (adjourned meeting set)
carryover.effect: resume at point of interruption next meeting
pending question -> unfinished-business(a); unreached orders -> unfinished categories (b)/(c); unreached special orders -> special-orders-unfinished
everything temporarily-disposed falls to ground except matters in committee hands
unreached items carry to next meeting ahead of that meeting's items, absent special provision and special-order conflict

carryover.case: bylaws-mandated item not reached in its required session
carryover.effect: carries as unfinished business/special order if next regular meeting within quarterly-interval

agenda_overlay: When an agenda or program is adopted it BECOMES the order of business for the session [41:61, 59:48]: hour-assigned items are special orders unless marked guidance-only; unassigned items are general orders [41:58]. Adoption/change thresholds: rules.json change_thresholds agenda-program row. At an item's assigned hour the chair announces it, puts pending questions to vote without further debate (subject to immediate table/postpone/refer motions, undebatable in that posture, and a two-thirds extension motion) [41:65]. Precirculated but unadopted agendas bind nothing [41:62].
